title: Choose the look for the brew-day screen
question: This is the direction I'd build: kettle dials. Keep it, take one of the alternates, or ask for a fresh set.

options.label: Kettle dials
options.lineage: The dial thermometer on a brew kettle, with an instrument's setpoint marker
options.thesis: Each vessel is the dial you already read on the kettle: a needle for actual, a marker on the rim for target.
options.viewport: Three big dials in rig order (HLT, mash tun, boil kettle), big actual and target digits under each, labelled switches with lamps, and the current step along the bottom.
options.risk: Dials need room: three must fit a desktop screen with their controls, and on a phone they drop to one per row.

options.label: Safety-yellow signage
options.lineage: Airport overhead sign bands, fused with brewery safety marking
options.thesis: Each vessel hangs under a yellow sign band with its temperature at gate-number size and one message: what it's doing and what's next.
options.viewport: Three yellow bands across the top with huge black temperatures; arrows show the flow from HLT to mash to boil; the next step is the biggest message.
options.risk: Yellow fills the screen, so warnings need a different signal, and it reads as plant signage more than kettle hardware.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: huge numbers read from anywhere in the garage, but it speaks an airport's language, not a brewery's.

options.label: One temperature rail
options.lineage: A spectrograph's calibrated rail, fused with the HERMS
options.thesis: All three vessels sit on one shared temperature scale, so you see the HLT running ahead of the mash at a glance.
options.viewport: One long rail across the screen from 60 to 215 °F; each vessel's actual and target are lines on it, with big digits above.
options.risk: State lives in hairlines (solid, dashed, doubled) that fade from across the garage, and it looks like lab gear, not brewing kit.
options.case: Fuses poorly because hairline state vanishes at a distance; the shared scale is the idea worth keeping.

options.label: Dot-matrix readouts
options.lineage: Emigre's bitmap type specimens, fused with controller LED displays
options.thesis: Temperatures set in coarse pixel numerals at poster size, like a controller's dot-matrix display blown up.
options.viewport: Huge pixel-numeral temperatures for each vessel in a ruled grid, with red kept for anything switched on.
options.risk: It reads as 1990s graphic design rather than equipment, and its type-specimen grammar has nothing to switch or sequence.
options.case: Fuses awkwardly: the pixel numerals echo controller displays, but the rest of its grammar is editorial.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What brewing-controller apps ship: vessel cards, a step list and a chart, done well.
canonCard.viewport: Three vessel cards across the top with toggles, the step list at the side, a temperature chart below.
canonCard.risk: Familiar and the quickest to build; it is also the closest to the generic web-app look you said would feel wrong.
